name: stefs-plugins
description: Stef's Claude Code plugins — conventions for building prototypes and proof-of-concept projects, the documentation and planning conventions that sit beside them, and general-purpose utilities and conventions.

plugins.name: prototype-conventions
plugins.description: Conventions and guidelines for building prototypes and proof-of-concept projects — not for production use. Five skills: SPA frontends, Terraform/AWS infrastructure, Go and Node Lambdas, and product requirements. How a project records its own conventions, and the documentation, proposal, plan-of-action and glossary rules, are in the sibling documentation-and-planning plugin; general API design and MySQL conventions are in utils. Every skill is model-invoked on topic match; the plugin registers no hooks and adds no executable code.

plugins.name: documentation-and-planning
plugins.description: Four skills carrying the portable layer of documentation and planning conventions: conventions (how a project records its own rules in conventions/, the two-layer model, and precedence), documentation (the markdown rules every document follows, including an up-to-date table of contents; the three tenses of architecture/, instructions/ and proposals/; API docs, READMEs, diagrams and writing proposals), plan-of-action (the staged implementation plan a settled proposal becomes, and carrying it out stage by stage), and glossary (one file per term, linked rather than restated). Model-invoked on topic match; the plugin registers no hooks and adds no executable code.

plugins.name: utils
plugins.description: General-purpose utility commands, skills and agents for Claude Code, plus general conventions that are not specific to prototypes: api-design (HTTP/JSON URLs, payloads, list endpoints with filter[...], q and page-based pagination, 400 versus 422 errors, resource-suffix versioning) and mysql (schema naming, UUIDv7 keys, timestamps, migrations and SQL formatting). Includes the default-on auto-summary-commit workflow: a pair of hooks commits the prompt and its summary at the end of every turn that changed files, scoped to the paths that turn actually changed.
